subject: brms compiles correctly, but won't compile model when attempting to run on our HPC

messages.author: 1a43ff58a2fb9d9e
messages.subject: brms compiles correctly, but won't compile model when attempting to run on our HPC
parts:
Hello!

A researcher I'm assisting, would like to use brms to run some analyses. I am able to successfully compile the brms, via "install.packages('brms')", but when the researcher or I try to run the analysis through our job queue system (SGE), we receive this error in the output file:

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) :
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! icpc: error #10001: could not find directory in which g++ resides
make: *** [file57e47f1e4ec4.o] Error 1
Calls: brm ... <Anonymous> -> cxxfunctionplus -> cxxfunction -> compileCode
In addition: Warning message:
running command '/usr/local/R/3.4.0-intel17.0.2/lib64/R/bin/R CMD SHLIB file57e47f1e4ec4.cpp 2> file57e47f1e4ec4.cpp.err.txt' had status 1
Execution halted

This was with R version 3.4.0, compiled with the Intel compiler, and the latest version of brms, on RHEL 7.3.

The same error happened when trying to run R 3.3.3 compiled with GCC 4.8.5.

I've seen a solution, for Rstudio, which involves installing Rtools, but we're on Linux and Rtools is only for Windows.

Did I miss a configuration item for brms or R? Or...?

Thanks for any insight that is possible!

Ben

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: brms compiles correctly, but won't compile model when attempting to run on our HPC
parts:
Hi Ben,

it seems as if Stan (the backend of brms) does not find the C++ compiler of your linux system. I suggest that you ask this question on the Stan users forum (http://discourse.mc-stan.org/), since it is Stan and not brms related.

All the best,
Paul
